# Mother, Assumption and chiasm

## #0

<a id="mother-encounter"></a>

The Mother flow begins with a body received, a body bearing another, and the receiving body itself returned. Taylor's encounter with the cope at St Bridget's in Skenfrith brings this movement into a particular gathering of images: Mary being lifted, figures perceived as rabbits beside her, six-winged seraphic forms, wheels, and eagles with two heads. His recollection of Jung's Assumption discussion meets a native relation already established in his work: the three recognised as one, whose recognition has its own threefold articulation. The image becomes a place to work through that relation in embodiment.

In the [Skenfrith dialogue](../../../../episteme/sources/internal-corpus/taylor/chat-logs/taylor-2026-skenfrith-cope-jung-ql/taylor-2026-skenfrith-cope-jung-ql.md), Taylor’s corrections change how the images are read. His opening observation initiates the inquiry; the assistant proposes relations; Taylor rejects pairings which lose his notation’s established operations. The complete local conversation keeps these differences consequential. An identification of the embroidered figure answers to the object, while the interpretation of Taylor’s notation answers to his correction.

The rabbit belongs first to the encounter. Taylor reports seeing rabbits lifting Mary; the assistant identifies supporting angels and invokes an unnamed description of the cope. The experienced figure initiates an interpretation which remains answerable to the object. A further object witness could change how that figure is identified and, with it, the relation the image makes available. The ambiguity keeps perceiving, interpreting and intended iconography distinct in this actual encounter.

Taylor also recalls inquiry into the surrounding power dynamics. The assistant expands this into a history of castles, lordship and imperial imagery. The later Mother-flow correction returns the encounter to its actual occasion: a personal visit which opens the Mother flow, Assumption and chiasm. The site locates that encounter; the symbolic movement concerns the maternal body and its recognitional return.

Within this encounter, Mary remains a particular mother. Biblical Mary, the mother of Jesus, gives the later maternal reception its name and body. The Assumption develops through a later doctrinal and interpretive history. Jung’s psychological reception and Taylor’s chiasm carry that maternal relation into further reflection, where each transformation retains the body through which it becomes possible.

## #1

<a id="mother-body-received"></a>

The incarnation–Assumption movement has two directions. In the first, the maternal matrix receives the Logos into bodily life. What is articulated as divine Word comes through a body which bears it. In the return, that maternal body is itself received. The condition of embodiment remains present in what is recognised as whole. This is the force of the quilt's correction, assumption-*of* rather than ascent-*away-from*: return bears what made manifestation possible instead of treating that condition as a vessel to discard once its work has been done.

Mary is both the receiving matrix and the bodily figure received. If only a general feminine principle entered the final account, the particular body that bore the relation would disappear just where recognition claims completion. The chiasm retains that body across the change of direction. Mother, child, receiving and being received remain different relations within the circulation; their difference gives the crossing something to carry.

Jung’s *Answer to Job* develops a particular psychological reception of this embodied return. His [Sophia and Assumption sequence](../../../../episteme/sources/psychology/jung/jung-1969-psychology-religion-cw11/jung-1969-psychology-religion-cw11.md), §§609–617,625–628 and746–757 with their intervening and adjacent context, moves through wisdom, incarnation, perfection/completeness, maternal reception and conscious individuation. Each turn changes the preceding God-image rather than adding a general feminine principle to an unchanged account.

Jung begins this Sophia movement by turning from Job toward Wisdom in other texts. In §609 he takes up the pre-existent feminine wisdom of Proverbs; §610 relates Sophia to Hebrew Chochma and the Johannine Logos while invoking Indian Śakti as a comparison. The discussion then passes through Ecclesiasticus and the Wisdom of Solomon. Speaking, pervading, world-building, loving, guiding and reflecting give Sophia more than a generic receptive property. These are Jung's readings of several textual witnesses, not biblical Wisdom gathered from Job alone. His historical proposals about contact and descent retain their own evidential burden. [CW11 §§609–613](../../../../episteme/sources/psychology/jung/jung-1969-psychology-religion-cw11/jung-1969-psychology-religion-cw11.md).

The sequence returns to the tested righteous person. Jung brings the oppression of the righteous in the Wisdom of Solomon beside Job, then reads Yahweh's behaviour as a crisis of faithfulness and self-knowledge. Sophia's remembrance answers the demand for divine self-reflection: the human being's knowledge of God becomes consequential for the God-image. The argument moves through an interpretation of creation and its familial counterparts toward a changed incarnation. In §625 the Second Eve has temporal and material priority: the God-man is to be born through a woman. Mary receives the appointment of Sophia's embodiment, friend and intercessor, while Christ is related to the pre-existent Logos and the figure of the master workman. Jung explicitly develops the mother–son relation through that shared symbolic office. [CW11 §§614–628](../../../../episteme/sources/psychology/jung/jung-1969-psychology-religion-cw11/jung-1969-psychology-religion-cw11.md).

Jung’s image of completion also exposes a difficulty within its own reception. In §§626–627 Jung argues that the exceptional protections surrounding Mary can separate her from ordinary humanity. Perfection brought close to Christ can impair the feminine completeness meant to compensate it; an incarnation protected from the actual human condition risks being only partial. This is Jung's psychological critique of the doctrine as he reads it. It is not the Church's account of its own teaching, and his accompanying generalisations about men and women do not become the native meaning of Taylor's poles. The tension matters to the Mother flow: exaltation can either receive embodied life or produce an ideal too purified to bear it. [CW11 §§625–628](../../../../episteme/sources/psychology/jung/jung-1969-psychology-religion-cw11/jung-1969-psychology-religion-cw11.md).

The later Assumption discussion follows the burden of continuing incarnation in the empirical creature. Jung interprets the longing for a maternal intercessor, the heavenly bride and the marriage imagery as a movement toward further incarnation. Recognition and declaration by human beings enter its temporal fulfilment. He insists upon personal feminine representation, yet expressly distinguishes his psychological reading from a dogmatic assertion that Mary has become a goddess. The argument then moves into conscious individuation: the person encounters the unconscious, recognises its opposites and takes responsibility for a relation whose process would otherwise remain obscure. Psychological efficacy is real for Jung; it does not license a simple identification of God with the unconscious as a whole. [CW11 §§746–757](../../../../episteme/sources/psychology/jung/jung-1969-psychology-religion-cw11/jung-1969-psychology-religion-cw11.md).

The maternal body is received through differentiated relations. Sophia, biblical Mary, the mother in Jung’s reconstruction and Taylor’s embodied return give wisdom, incarnation and recognition different offices. Jung’s perfection/completeness difficulty remains active: an ideal too purified to bear ordinary embodied life can fail at the very completion it announces. In [*Aion*](../../../../episteme/sources/psychology/jung/jung-1978-aion-cw9-2/jung-1978-aion-cw9-2.md), Self, Christ-symbolism, opposites and symbolic totality develop through another sequence. Their meeting in Taylor’s recollection lets the maternal return be read through these different movements.

<a id="mother-sophia-logos-shakti"></a>

The Sophia–Logos–Śakti comparison opens three distinguishable tasks: knowing and recognising, articulating form, and the power of manifestation. In the assistant’s proposed account, Sophia carries recognitional wisdom, Logos the intelligibility of articulated form, and Śakti the power through which the relation acts. Taylor’s invitation to explore Jung’s comparison makes this an inquiry into how recognition, articulation and manifestation cooperate. Jung’s §610 relates essential qualities and evokes Śakti; the three-office allocation is a further proposed differentiation whose adequacy depends upon what each name’s source account actually does.

The Śakti relation matters because receiving and recognising already act. A matrix does not become operative only when a supposedly active term arrives from elsewhere. [Luminous appearing and reflexive power](../../../../../section-rooms/arguments/A05-Prakasa-Vimarsa.md) distinguish through their [inseparable relation](../../../../../section-rooms/arguments/concepts/C13-Prakasa-Vimarsa.md). The maternal crossing makes active reception tangible: bearing lets articulation become embodied, and recognition can transform the bearer’s relation to what appears.

## #2

<a id="mother-chiasm"></a>

Taylor's correction identifies the live pressure: the functional masculine and feminine reading crosses the previously given physical and mental poles. Articulation, differentiation and explication give the `1–2–3` block a masculine operation in this reading. Receiving, containing, reflecting and gathering give `4–5–0` a feminine operation. Yet the older symbolic assignment being examined associates physical matter and nature with the feminine, and mental or spiritual life with the masculine. Reading what a pole does and reading the field it bears produce different gender valences.

The chiasm preserves both relations as the object of inquiry. The first block can be read as masculine articulation in a feminine material field; the second as feminine recognition in a masculine mental field. These are symbolic assignments whose crossing is being developed, not determinations of what men and women essentially are. They cannot be stabilised by treating one assignment as the literal meaning of the numbers. Each pole's operation already reaches into the field conventionally attributed to the other.

Christ–Logos and Mary give this crossing a body. Spiritual articulation becomes embodied; the embodied mother is received into spiritual recognition. The directions remain distinguishable even as each makes the other intelligible. If embodiment were only a descent to be reversed, the return would undo the very relation it completes. If recognition retained only an image of the mother, her bodily condition would disappear from the proclaimed whole. The Mother flow returns bodily and recognitionally together: what made manifestation possible is received within its completion.

[Neumann’s developmental morphology](../../../../episteme/sources/psychology/neumann/neumann-1954-origins-history-consciousness/neumann-1954-origins-history-consciousness.md) differentiates bodily dependence, nourishment, engulfment, separation and a transformed relation to the mother. Nourishing reception sustains a life’s differentiation; consuming reception closes that possibility within the receiver. The maternal image can bear both relations. Their actual bearer and history make the distinction consequential: a particular mother or goddess has to be encountered through what she does in her whole telling.

The need and Desire comparison asks a further question of these nourishing and devouring faces. Does reception sustain another life as other, or consume it within the receiver’s satisfaction? The question matters locally to a body received rather than discarded. A common doctrinal identity would require more than this shared question; the proposed comparison follows the actual relation of sustaining, differentiating and receiving before it can judge that stronger claim.

<a id="mother-three-recognised"></a>

The native `3:1 = 3:3` gives recognition its articulated office. Taylor states at the opening that the one in `3:1` is the three encapsulated or recognised. The first block, `1–2–3`, is known through `4–5–0`: void, unity and their paradoxical `0/1` oneness. The one is thus the unitive condition of the three, whose recognitional constitution can itself be unfolded. It is neither an extra count appended without relation nor a featureless terminus. The second three disclose what the recognising one does.

The Mother image makes this operation felt through matrix, mediation and recognition. Receiving gives the articulated life somewhere to arise; bearing sustains its differentiation; recognition receives that differentiation as belonging to a whole. The body persists on return, so the recognitional pole remains related to what it had to bear. The unitive one opens through the threefold work of recognising, keeping `3:1 = 3:3` active in the embodied encounter.

## #3

<a id="mother-wheels-wings"></a>

The two wheels give the crossing a second form. Taylor directs attention to the full sequence `0/1 → 1/0 → (0/1)/(1/0)`. A first orientation meets its inverse; their relation becomes explicit. The wheel need not be reduced to an isolated zero. The complete orientation already relates the singular One and manifest All, and its inverse changes how that relation is encountered. The outer slash retains the orientations in operative self-difference. It does not divide numerical quantities by zero.

As an encountered image, a wheel permits changing orientation while its whole form persists. Two wheels can then bear conjugate orientations within one relation. The movement through one view and its inverse differs from holding their relation together. The final compound matters because the whole can now carry the reversal it underwent. [The two Ones](../../../../../section-rooms/arguments/A11-The-Two-Ones-0-One-1-All.md) and [their reciprocal offices](../../../../../section-rooms/arguments/concepts/C49-The-Two-Ones-0-One-1-All.md) keep One and All differentiated; [Arche-Topos](../../../../../section-rooms/arguments/A16-Arche-Topos-as-Differential-Field.md) develops orientation as a relation through which positions become possible. The wheel gives this changing view a persisting body.

The seraphic forms give that orientation a sixfold articulation. Taylor reports six wings and asks after `3:3`; the assistant develops two wheel-bearing six-winged forms as a conjugate pair. The whole visual reading can hold one sixfold and its primed counterpart, `6` and `6′`, while each retains the two blocks `(1,2,3):(4,5,0)`. A single body is the condition through which the wings belong together. It does not add a seventh wing, and a second body does not make the first six a series of unrelated numbered items. The proposed `6+6′` develops two articulations in relation; exact historical details of the cope still require their object witness.

The dialogue's first attempt to map the wings into vertical pairs is explicitly corrected. Taylor rejects `2↔5` and `3↔0`; only `1↔4` belongs to the established pairings in that proposed arrangement. The native complementary folds are `0↔5`, `1↔4` and `2↔3`. They have their own harmonic work and cannot be manufactured by placing the two recognitional blocks into adjacent columns. The body can sustain both the `3:3` reading and the native complementary relations without pretending they are the same partition. The important operation here is blockwise and recursive recognition.

The assistant’s invocation of Isaiah’s wing functions and Ezekiel’s intersecting wheels proposes another comparison. Here the encountered wing-and-wheel relation keeps its actual symbolic work: a body bears differentiated wings, and changing orientation returns through that body. Their scriptural and iconographic combination requires the particular textual and object witnesses before it can be read as an historical programme.

This return to the wheel and wing preserves the Mother movement. The body that bears the differentiation remains its condition when the differentiation is recognised. Recognition opens the one rather than evacuating it. In the Assumption chiasm, the same pressure prevents the maternal body from vanishing into a final spiritual account of what it supposedly meant.

## #4

<a id="mother-eagle-valence"></a>

The eagle changes the operative question. Its two heads direct one body toward opposed orientations, but the governing relation here is signed valence and power. Taylor corrects the assistant's attempt to give the eagle the wheels' Spanda equations and a `1/1` reconciliation. He had pointed to `−1` and `+1`, and to the difference between a relation retaining their polarity and operations that cancel or amplify through negation. The one body does not establish in advance that its power is reconciled.

The retained form is `(-1)/(+1)`. Each pole keeps its sign across the relation. Ordinary addition, `(-1)+(+1)=0`, cancels the signed quantities; subtraction produces `(-1)-(+1)=-2`, while the inverse subtraction gives `(+1)-(-1)=+2`. These are three distinct arithmetic results. Taylor's authored political and psychic reading uses them to distinguish held polarity, cancellation and one valence's amplification through negation of the other. The sign of a pole does not, by itself, determine its moral worth.

The eagle's power-body can consequently be asked which operation it carries. Does its unity retain opposed orientations in relation? Does an apparent agreement cancel their difference? Does one direction acquire its enlarged power by negating the other? Those questions give the shared body an accountable office. They also prevent the Mother flow from ending in a picture where completion means that the differentiated life has disappeared. The same whole that receives must be able to sustain a difference within what it receives.

[The two logics](../../../../../section-rooms/arguments/A13-Two-Logics-of-Two-Dia-Syn.md) and [Dia / Syn](../../../../../section-rooms/arguments/concepts/C50-Dia-Syn.md) distinguish what the eagle’s common body can carry. Dia gives difference a determinate orientation; Syn keeps the relation through which differentiated terms can be recomposed and returned. Healthy polarity holds signed difference together. Addition cancels it; directed subtraction magnifies one valence through negating the other. The power-body becomes legible through which operation actually acts, rather than through an appearance of unity alone.

Taylor’s signed-valence correction changes the interpretation of the eagle. Its two heads now prompt an inquiry into power’s operation within one body: held polarity, cancellation or amplification through negating another. The journey gives that inquiry its encountered image, while the quilt’s Mother-flow correction keeps bodily and recognitional return as its direction.

## #5→0

In [Neumann’s maternal relation](../../../archetypal-ground/neumann-images/WHOLE.md#neumann-metabolism), nourishment lets a received life become differentiated and capable of another relation. Taylor’s chiasm keeps the maternal body within what returns. Incarnation and Assumption reverse receiving and being received; Jung’s reception of the 1950 declaration brings that movement into psychological reflection; Taylor’s later encounter makes it a place of corrected recognition. Their temporal differences give the return its concrete bearers.

<a id="mother-native-return"></a>

The completed constellation returns through distinct offices. Wheels carry inverse orientations and their recognised relation. Wings articulate the three through the three that know them, with their bodily coherence intact. The eagle carries the signed alternatives of power. The Mother flow crosses embodiment and recognition while receiving the maternal body in its return. These relations can act together because they have not been reduced to one number, one sex assignment or one emblem of undifferentiated divinity.

The [eight determinations](../../../../../section-rooms/arguments/A18-Primordial-Symbolon-and-Its-Eight-Determinations.md) unfold `/ = −/− → 0/1 → ?/! → −/+ → X/x → AM/IS → ∞/dx → 1/0`. Under their prior relating stroke, a determination becomes available, is questioned, bears a signed relation, manifests determining capacity through a particular, reaches personed presence and effects an exact difference before returning to its source. The [native core](../../../../episteme/sources/internal-corpus/taylor/taylor-2026-core-theorems-pithy/taylor-2026-core-theorems-pithy.md) derives that whole traversal with its inversions and relations. Sixfold recognition through the cope articulates the knowing relation in this embodied encounter. `X/x` distinguishes the determining capacity from the particular maternal image through which it becomes legible.

The Name series—Name, Truth, Mind, Word, Logos, Son, Image—retains its coequal Power relation—Power, Play, Need, Sacrifice, Decision, Love, Work. An articulated name or image has been borne, sustained and brought into life; recognition returns upon that bearing. The Mother chiasm makes their conjunction concrete. Logos and Son acquire embodied force through matrix, labour and consequence. The achieved image keeps this cooperation available when what bore it is received into the whole.

The [tattvic differential field](../../../../../section-rooms/arguments/A09-Tattvic-Differential-Field.md) gives manifestation a source-related genealogy of local capacities. Recognition changes the relation to embodiment while retaining the differentiated world. [Reflexive appearing](../../../../../section-rooms/arguments/A05-Prakasa-Vimarsa.md) and [its active power](../../../../../section-rooms/arguments/concepts/C13-Prakasa-Vimarsa.md) keep receiving distinct from a passive second image. The maternal crossing follows the same practical pressure through its own body: receiving and recognising act upon a relation whose differentiated life persists.

<a id="mother-image-recognition-return"></a>

A maternal image can organise dependence, fear, protection, receptivity or a claim to possess what it bears. Its [local valuation](../../../../../section-rooms/arguments/A19-Complex-as-Local-Arbitration-Regime.md) belongs to a [lived affective organisation](../../../../../section-rooms/arguments/concepts/C31-Complex.md). The same visible figure can therefore have different consequences through the relation actually lived. [Archetype](../../../../../section-rooms/arguments/concepts/C32-Archetype.md) differentiates that particular image from the determining capacity made legible through it. Neumann’s morphology follows another set of whole transformations; the cope’s encounter gives this image its own body and history.

[Image, valuation and possession](../../../../../section-rooms/arguments/A20-Image-Valuation-Possession.md) diverge where recognition either restores the body’s standing or replaces it with an authoritative image of what the body is for. A [living symbol](../../../../../section-rooms/arguments/concepts/C21-Living-Symbol-Idol.md) keeps its represented life able to answer. The angel/rabbit ambiguity gives this relation a modest exact test: the experienced image remains correctable through encounter with the object. The Assumption chiasm makes the same obligation bodily: the recognised whole retains the condition it receives. [Individuation and recognition](../../../../../section-rooms/arguments/A21-Individuation-Recognition.md) change the relation to embodied dependence, allowing differentiation to succeed without turning its sustaining relation into possession.

<a id="mother-bearing-return"></a>

The body changes what a return owes. A [mediating office](../../../../../section-rooms/arguments/A25-Covenant-Mediating-Office-Source-Authority.md) bears consequential work within a field it did not originate. Matrix, mediator and recogniser perform real work; receiving their result owes recognition to the relation through which it arrived. [Delegated labour](../../../../../section-rooms/arguments/A29-Power-Delegated-Labour-Return.md) carries the corresponding obligation into a commission: encountered cost, resistance and possibility can reach the office which governs the next act. The Mother flow makes the sustaining body present within completion, so the received product cannot hide what bore it.

[Trust](../../../../../section-rooms/arguments/A23-Trust-Faith-and-the-Formal-Limit.md) continues through reliance that precedes an exhaustive account of what bears it. The mother/child relation gives that received dependence a body; its return keeps dependence distinct from ownership. [Unity without possession](../../../../../section-rooms/arguments/A27-Self-and-Other-Unity-without-Possession.md) holds this difference: a life borne within a relation remains capable of answering beyond its bearer’s account. [Compassion](../../../../../section-rooms/arguments/A35-Compassion-Sensitivity-to-Origins-Epi-Logos-as-Vocation.md) directs care toward the body, history and work through which the achieved form became possible. Recognising those conditions returns responsibility to them; bodily suffering supplies no necessary price of completion.

<a id="mother-comparison-return"></a>

[Homological agreement and analogical proportion](../../../../episteme/etymologies/homology-and-analogy/WHOLE-FIELD-homology-and-analogy.md) compare what changes, what is retained and what returns through maternal body, recognitional triads, inverse wheels and signed power. The body persists across reversed reception; the recognitional one opens through its threefold activity; inverse views remain related; signed poles differ through the operation performed. Numerical recurrence can suggest these crossings, while the complete relations give each comparison its warrant. [Symbol, Account and Trust](../../../../episteme/etymologies/symbol-account-and-trust/WHOLE-FIELD-symbol-account-and-trust.md) hold their return together. The encountered form discloses; its account remains answerable to source; trust carries it into inquiry; the resulting interpretation becomes a condition of the next encounter. Taylor’s correction enacts this circuit when the account of wings and eagle changes through what it had misread.

[Devotion to the whole and the particular aperture](../../../../episteme/sources/internal-corpus/taylor/taylor-2026-definition-god-draft3/taylor-2026-definition-god-draft3.md) gives this return its double obligation. [Integral zero](../../../../../section-rooms/arguments/A36-Advent-of-Integral-Zero.md) receives an achieved determination through its exceeding source-relation. In the Mother flow, recognition receives the matrix within the whole it bore; the completed account returns to the particular body instead of abandoning it as the price of completion. A further inquiry can retain the interpretation with reasons or correct the answer, model, source or governing condition the new encounter exposes. Where an interpreting agent compares an image with a witness, it is the local functional knower; image and witness are known; memory, comparison rule and instruments are means. The same interpreting apparatus belongs among the means of the person’s containing inquiry. Its later act must inherit the warranted correction or retention while the encountered body remains able to answer.

## Source standing

The Skenfrith conversation is provenance of Taylor’s thinking and corrections. Rabbit/angel identification, the cope’s making and its intended iconographic programme require an object witness; lunar, fertility or resurrection symbolism cannot be attributed to a medieval rabbit whose identification remains unverified; the assistant’s castle and imperial history remains unverified. The quilt explicitly re-keys the visit as personal and the essay relation as Mother flow, Assumption and chiasm. Isaiah/Ezekiel wing-and-wheel parallels require their own selected primary passages. The encountered geometry gives inverse orientations a symbolic body without proving a geometric theorem.

The Assumption’s official definition has no selected Gospel witness in this account. The locally held Hull second-edition *Psychology and Religion: West and East* supplies the selected *Answer to Job* primary spans and six source-matched paraphrase cards. The account uses numbered paragraphs with their stated context; exact quotation wording and newly verified print-page citations are not claimed. Jung’s Sophia discussion gathers Proverbs, Ecclesiasticus and Wisdom of Solomon, rather than finding their entire sequence in Job. His comparison with Śakti and his historical contact proposals retain distinct evidential obligations. His psychological reception of Mary and Assumption is not an official four-person Trinity or a dogmatic identification of Mary as a goddess. The Sophia–Logos–Śakti three-office formula remains a proposed comparison, not a fixed source doctrine or a Mary-tattva assignment.

The separate *Aion* house retains contextual paraphrases from the consulted 1979 paperback; collation against the selected 1978 hardcover and verification of quotation remain Open. Neumann’s morphology, Levinasian need/Desire and the Christian maternal reception have their own source sequences. Their relation is tested through the sustained operations above; common historical descent or doctrine needs separate evidence. The corrected signed eagle retains `(-1)/(+1)`, distinct addition/subtractions and no automatic moral identity for a sign.
